data.name: Jivanta
data.gender_notes: Jivanta is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jivanta is derived from the Sanskrit word 'jiv' which means 'living' or 'conscious'. It is a name given to those who are believed to have a vibrant and lively spirit. The name is often used in Hindu mythology to refer to various deities and figures who embody the essence of life and consciousness. The name Jivanta carries the meaning “Living, Conscious, Vibrant” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jivanta usually hope their child will grow to embody living, conscious, vibrant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that embodies the essence of life and consciousness.
data.etymology: Jivanta belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Living, Conscious, Vibrant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jivanta total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

It carries a powerful significance as a name that speaks to the vitality and spirit of an individual, emphasizing the importance of living fully and embracing the energy of life.
data.spiritual_significance: Jivanta is more than just a name; it is a manifestation of the divine that reminds us of the eternal nature of the soul. It inspires us to honor the gift of life and cultivate a deep awareness of the consciousness that drives us. By embracing the spirit of Jivanta, we can live a more fulfilled and joyful life, connected to the help of the divine Force.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Jivanta signifies a person who is full of life and energy, continually pulsating with the divine force of existence. It is a name that invokes the spirit of vitality and zest for living.

historical_references.reference: According to Hindu mythology, Jivanta was a divine serpent who was the son of the sage Vasishtha and the goddess Arundhati. He is also known as Jatayu and is revered as a protector of Rama and Sita during their exile in the forest.

Another reference to Jivanta can be found in the Jain scriptures, where he is mentioned as a celestial being who attained Kevala Jnana, the highest form of spiritual knowledge. Jivanta is also regarded as a symbol of longevity and vitality in Jainism.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Jivanta' is of Hindu origin and translates to 'living' or 'one who is alive'. In today's context, it is commonly associated with practices and philosophies that promote a holistic and vibrant life. Jivanta is seen on various modern platforms such as Instagram, YouTube, and Pinterest, where individuals and communities share content related to Ayurveda, Yoga, and Spirituality, emphasizing the importance of living an engaged, healthy, and mindful life.

name_in_real_life.story: Maya Jivanta, a teacher in Bali, Indonesia, shares that their name Jivanta meaning "Living, Conscious, Vibrant" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.
